state-invariants-the-cage-keeps.text: A table of 7 rows, columns invariant, statement. The rows: pins; admissibility; admission; delta; custody; destination; coverage.

namings-redeemers-contract-change-declar.text: A table of 3 rows, columns purpose, constructors after this ticket. The rows: application spend; application mint; witness mint.

cagedatum-constructor-appended.text: The cage datum keeps RequestDatum at index zero and StateDatum at index one, and appends AbsentCustody at index two with key and refund fields.
RequestDatum is spent through Contribute at the ordinary request validator. The cage state validator gains no RequestDatum spending arm.

the-leaf.text: A table of 3 rows, columns state, byte. The rows: Absent; Active; Terminal.
Any other value bytes are refused before a proof is checked. The naming-era values — the representative name, the over marker — are not leaves.

token-identity.text: Under each of the three policies the asset name is the registry key. Identity is (policy, key). A key recreated after Delete(0x01) carries the same identity.

state-eight-fields-replaces-six.text: A table of 8 rows, columns field, role, change. The rows: root; tip; process_time; retract_time; application_policy; active_policy; absent_policy; terminal_policy.
consumer_pin is deleted. All four policies are set at genesis and preserved by every Modify.

operation-indices-published-read-appende.text: A table of 4 rows, columns index, constructor, fields. The rows: 0; 1; 2; 3.

the-approval.text: Minted under application_policy, quantity 1, asset name blake2b_256(edge ‖ key ‖ owner ‖ destination); edge one byte, the C2 row index (0 insertAbsent … 5 deleteActive). Carried by the request UTxO; recomputed by the cage; not burned at fold.

request-field-appended.text: The request appends a destination address and inline-datum hash to its existing fields. A minted active or terminal token must arrive there. For an absent insertion, the address instead names the refund recipient.

A retirement completion request carries the same registry's seed-derived cage token and lives at its ordinary request validator, applied to that token and state policy. The validator identity is not chosen in a request or redeemer.

naming-application-parameters-and-pendin.text: The naming application has an immutable applied request-validator hash. Derive the cage token from an existing seed output reference, apply the ordinary request validator to that token and the parameterless state policy, then apply the naming application. Genesis pins the resulting application policy.

Retirement records the validator hash, same-registry request token and approved active-to-terminal request, and moves the active token into completion custody while the leaf remains active. Completion validates and consumes that stored request, removes the active holding and writes terminal.
